The Hong Kong national security law, passed in Beijing, came into force on 30 June 2020. It made secession, subversion, terrorism and collusion with foreign forces crimes punishable by up to life in prison.

It was Beijing's answer to the protests of 2019. It let mainland security agents work in the city and allowed some cases to be tried on the mainland.

Within a few years nearly all opposition leaders were jailed or in exile, including the 47 democrats arrested for holding a primary election. The newspaper Apple Daily and its owner Jimmy Lai were prosecuted, and many civil groups shut down. Hundreds of thousands left, many for Britain under a special visa. Critics say it broke the promises of the Joint Declaration; the governments of China and Hong Kong say it restored order after the Umbrella years.
sum: The Hong Kong national security law, passed in Beijing, came into force on 30 June 2020. It made secession, subversion, terrorism and collusion with foreign forces crimes punishable by up to life in prison.
